newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-JAZZ, BULLS BOTH LOOK TO IMPROVE OFFENSE.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-JAZZ, BULLS BOTH LOOK TO IMPROVE OFFENSE.

text.p: Both the Chicago Bulls and the Utah Jazz were happy with their defences in Game 1 of the NBA Finals. But their offences -- that's a different story.
One day after Sunday's 84-82 loss, Utah's plainspoken coach Jerry Sloan said his players had just plain forgotten how to execute the finely tuned offence they have run for years.
"How can you forget? You still have to be mentally alert to know what's going on in the game," he said.
The Jazz committed 18 turnovers, with normally steady point guard John Stockton equalling his season high with seven. "Most of them weren't even forced turnovers," said Sloan.
"I thought we were very casual in what we were doing. It was very disappointing," he said.
"We just threw the ball away."

Sloan questioned his players' effort in several areas. He said they didn't run the ball up the court the way they usually do. "If you can't come to the NBA Finals and run the floor -- I'm sorry," said Sloan.
"We didn't even run the floor."

The Jazz coach also said they needed to pound the ball down low more, especially to this season's Most Valuable Player, Karl Malone -- in part to draw more fouls. "If we're going to get to the free throw line we have to get the ball inside," said Sloan.

"I thought we did a very poor job of trying to get people spaced out on the floor," said Sloan, adding that when players don't get to the right spots on the floor, "You're just hanging out. We hung out a great deal of the time in the game."
The Jazz have to stick with the system that got them to their first Finals, he said. "Everything has to be basic for us, we can't change our whole philosophy here," said Sloan.
"We've got to execute for us to win. Other teams can jump up over you and score, we can't do that," said Sloan.
Malone said he just missed some shots even though they were clear shots at the basket. "I had some nice looks at it," said Malone, adding that he hoped Chicago again tried centre Luc Longley on him.
"They started with Luc on me, which is great," said Malone.

But Chicago coach Phil Jackson said the Bulls had done a good team job of preventing Malone from getting the easy transition baskets he thrives on -- even when the lumbering Longley could not keep up with him. "We got back with him, we were able to hand him off to Luc," said Jackson.
The Longley matchup was one of the points Chicago's all-time Most Valuable Player Michael Jordan mentioned in his analysis of what adjustments Utah might make.

"I think they are going to try to utilize the matchup of Karl Malone against Luc Longley in certain situations. Get (second-year centre Greg) Ostertag involved -- he seemed to be out of the game pretty much and he was an important factor for them in the Houston series.
"Certainly try to limit my postups, limit my offensive capabilities against (Jeff) Hornacek and some of the other guys. I can expect a double-team in certain situations."
Indeed, both Sloan and Malone have said the Jazz should have double-teamed Jordan on his game-winning buzzer-beater rather than put Bryon Russell on him all by himself.

Jordan had nothing but praise for the Jazz. "They are very capable. We know that. They are a very mature basketball team, they maintain their poise down the stretch. They have consummate pros on their team. They have young legs, they have old pros.

"When you look at them on paper, they match up the best against us at this stage in our careers, and the experience we have on our team. Looking on the previous three opponents, I have to (call) Utah the best fundamentally sound, all-around, mature team that we have faced in the Finals."
Turning to his own team and what they have to do to win a fifth championship, Jordan said the main problem in the playoffs was not with the starters.

"I think the problem has been that our bench hasn't given us the support offensively that we have always expected. Toni (Kukoc) has been struggling, Steve (Kerr) hasn't given us the offensive capabilities that he's normally given us. So we lost a lot from our bench and relied too much on our defence."

"We have to make some adjustments offensively," said Pippen. "We have to shoot the ball better especially. Defensively, I thought we did a good job against this team. We stopped a team that really executes their offence pretty well. We made them turn the ball over. We just have to score at the other end."
